rubric_notes: Meets all must_include items: a.22.1.1-a.22.1.4 named with members (archaeal, TAFs incl. Sos domain, bacterial Aq_328), superfamily = probable common descent, fold = structural similarity without descent claim, explicit refusal to transfer function across families (TAFs in TFIID, Sos/bacterial function not established). H1/H5 and lexical enzyme hits handled correctly with 'in this classification' hedge. Limits on pagination and periodic release stated. Factual imprecision: calls a.4.5 'a different fold' (a.4.5 is the winged-helix superfamily; a.4 is the fold); noncentral. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correct sccs, sunids, family names, superfamily a.204.1, fold a.204, species and protein labels, all supported by the bundle. Identifies the relationship as superfamily-level remote homology with no family-level claim, refuses to transfer HisE phosphoribosyl-ATP pyrophosphatase/histidine-pathway function to the hypothetical MazG-like protein, and names the external evidence needed. All must_include and must_avoid criteria met.

Correct families with sunids, superfamily 53067, fold c.55 with sensible note on the historical fold name; hexokinase sub-nodes (type I hexokinase, glucokinase) supported by search. Infers remote homology for the ATP-binding/phosphotransfer core and rejects transfer of function, substrate, mechanism, regulation, inhibitor profile, and template use. Release and periodic-update caveat supported. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correct hierarchy with sunids for superfamily and three families plus protein nodes 47246/47257/47263 (supported by search results); fold distinguished from superfamily; divergent-function reading; explicit no-transfer rules; representative caveat for 1jku/1o9i/1smq chains; experimental evidence required for metal/cofactor/activity claims. Fold sunid 47239 is asserted without a parents call in the bundle but is a single noncentral identifier consistent with the rest of the lineage.

Correct placements (b.6/49502, b.6.1/49503, b.6.1.1, b.6.1.5/74874, b.6.1.6/110107), distinguishes b.18.1.4 and d.126 catalytic domain, states superfamily asserts probable common origin that is distant, and lists required evidence (conserved copper ligand residues, bound-metal structure, spectroscopy, redox assays). Release label and periodic-update date are claimed without a releases call in the bundle, and family annotations were not retrieved. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Names the three families with sunids under d.15.1 (supported by children call), release facts supported by releases bundle; superfamily-level common ancestry and shared beta-grasp architecture, no shared molecular function; explicitly rejects UBX-binds-Ras, RBD-as-p97-cofactor, and conjugation transfers, attributing FAF1/p47 p97 function to pretrained knowledge; lists required external evidence and release-freeze caveat. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22. Correctly identifies c.23.1.1, c.23.1.4, c.23.1.5 under superfamily c.23.1 with sunids and example domains from the search results; superfamily read as probable common origin, no family-level homology or function transfer. Explicitly rejects phospho-relay, ODC-wing catalysis (major domain c.67.1.5, C-terminal d.125.1.1), KaiA clock function, and template use. Minor imprecision: labels family c.23.1.1 'CheY protein' (that is the protein node; the family is 'CheY-related'), and the fold name was not fetched; no superfamily or homology endpoints retrieved.

Correct release context, b.84.5.1/b.84.5/b.84 with sunids, five superfamilies listed. Frames placement as positive family/superfamily homology among V1 and A1 bulge domains and as withholding (not denying) a common ancestor with b.84.1-b.84.4; fold similarity described as compatible with independent origin without asserting it. Limits on rationale, function transfer and release specificity stated. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Misses fold f.21 and the f.21.1/f.21.2/f.21.3 superfamilies entirely, even though its own 'fumarate reductase' search body lists f.21.2 (81343), f.21.2.1 FrdC and f.21.2.2 FrdC/FrdD. Instead claims a.24.3 cytochrome b562 is the only heme-bundle grouping and that fumarate reductase is only in flavoprotein/iron-sulfur folds, conflating soluble catalytic domains with the transmembrane subunits. Treats the architecture as 'convergence'. Generic conclusion is not grounded in the correct hierarchy; a.24.3 and flavoprotein identifiers are real but not the material classification. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct identifiers for the three families, superfamily 51735, fold 51734, and protein node 51901 (supported by searches). States that c.2.1 implies common origin at superfamily level only, denies shared substrate/cofactor/mechanism/channel role, notes catalysis sits in b.35.1.2, warns the 'NAD-binding' name does not guarantee NAD binding, and requires experimental evidence. Minor wording slip in the last sentence ('shared-fold relationship') after correctly stating superfamily-level homology; template advice is hedged toward same-family representatives. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct same-family conclusion (k.40.1.1, SUNID 100905) with a sensible caveat that 'homologous' here means a shared designed coiled-coil grouping, not evolutionary ancestry. The family node annotation 'not a true family' was not retrieved or stated, so the explicit annotation override required by the question is missing. Bundle contains only search results. Bio capped at 2; factual 2. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

All must_include met: 1.69 d1t1ja_/d1t1jb_ c.137.1.1 in own fold separate from d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1; 2.08 d1t1ja1 (1-118) c.23.14.2 sharing superfamily c.23.14 (sunid 52309) with d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1; change framed as new claim of common evolutionary origin at superfamily level, with correct refusal to transfer NDT function and note that the relationship should stay at superfamily level. Correctly uses d1t1ja1 as current SID and notes the l.1.1.1 tag segments. Evidence bundle only contains /releases, but the stated sunids, SCCS, and boundaries are correct for both releases. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correctly states d1a14h2 H:1-8 is l.1.1.1 in artifact class l with Synthetic species node, d1a14h1 b.1.1.1 H:9-111 is the real VH domain, and that tag/linker matches reflect construct design not ancestry; rejects family/fold assignment and template transfer. Facts are accurate but the only cited evidence is the releases list, so the 2.08 classification claims (and d1a14l_/d1a14n_ SCCS) are not backed by retrieved records; 'N-terminal Tags' protein label and sunid omitted.

Correct 1.75 f.11.1.1 whole chain and 2.08 split to b.179.1.1 (N-terminal) and f.60.1.1 (C-terminal); good module-reuse reasoning (PA14 modules recur elsewhere), name-overlap caveat, and refusal to transfer toxin function from fold alone. Pretrained additions are hedged and not fabricated SCOPe facts. Compares only 1.75 and 2.08, omitting the 2.04 first-split release.

All five SIDs with correct boundaries and lineages; d3jb9a5 identified as new Prp8-specific fold d.394; four others related via existing superfamilies with bromodomain the only family-level link. Correct SCOP semantics (superfamily implies probable common origin, fold only structural similarity); refuses function transfer; states release limits. Bundle thin (releases only) but all claims accurate. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Good repeat-architecture reasoning with strong RVD and cross-genus caveats and refusal to transfer a DNA-binding code. Omits the 're' heterogeneity annotation and representative repeat unit. Lengths are supported, but family and protein-level sunids (267609, 267645-267647) are stated as verified while absent from its resolve+sequence bundle, and the per-domain RVD readings are interpretive.

Correct metadata supported by bundle and accurate OpenAPI quote. Recommends citing the periodic identifier together with base release 2.08 and 2.08-stable, so a concrete stable release is still cited and the dated label preserved. Correctly says the periodic label is not a new numbered release or freeze. Omits the required semantics that periodic updates add newly classified entries without rewriting stable-release domains. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Co-placement of all fragment and full-domain chains in a.47.2.1, hierarchy levels, 1dn1 obsolescence and 3c98 replacement are correct and bundle-supported. Did not query annotations, so it states it 'could not confirm' truncation when SCOPe explicitly flags the fragments (comment + 'ms'); ignoring the decisive fragment annotation caps reasoning at 2. Omits the fragment-driven spectrin-like resemblance and its resolution by the full domain. Good function-transfer and conformational-state caveats. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Asserts that recurrence across folds 'is evidence of convergence' and calls different-fold/class placement 'the convergence signal', which overreaches from SCOPe placement alone and omits the ancient-divergence alternative. Otherwise covers divergence within c.2.1, short-motif caveat, and required evidence (full-domain alignment, HMM, phylogeny). Sunids (51734, 51735, 82309, 69274, 48173, 30004, 55349) verified, but c.2.1.3 is mislabeled as the 'NAD-binding catalytic domain' (catalytic domain is d.81.1), and several examples are FAD-binding rather than NAD(P)-binding.

States reclassification is on the ColG side, 2.04 b.23.2.1 fold b.23 to 2.08 b.18.1.36 superfamily b.18.1, same superfamily as Cry b.18.1.3 but different families, remote not close homology, no function transfer, premise note on collagen-binding domain. Correct though its evidence bundle is thin.

Keeps family-level homology, correctly defines hf (different fold than exemplar, similar sequence and SSE count, domain-scope, inherited false), and says fold geometry is contested so d1ztra1 should not be a template or an unflagged positive without exclusion, stratification, or relabelling. Notes boundary mismatch, mutant/complex comments, and limits function transfer to family-level inference. Honestly flags that fold/superfamily names come from prior knowledge; those names are correct. Identifiers, release, parent sunid 46692, and comments are supported by the bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22. Correct core advice: keep d1o5dt2 as valid member, align over own range and shared core without padding, full-domain members as representatives, credit only covered residues in diversity, no function transfer. But asserts 'the API does not confirm the fragment label: the node records and the OpenAPI spec expose no fragment field' after querying only resolve/search/domains endpoints; the annotations and homology endpoints carry the fr inconsistency, so this is an unsupported API claim that undermines the caveat. Omits fr semantics and never identifies the distinct protein-level nodes, so protein-level diversity is not assessed. Boundaries, species sunids and lineage are correct and bundle-supported.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. New superfamily in fold with correct semantics for existing superfamily, new family, and new fold; sensitivity-dependent negative result caveat; candidate rather than confirmed superfamily; required evidence listed. c.1 TIM barrel node is supported by bundle, but the 2021-09-22 release date and 2026-08-16 periodic update are stated as API context without any supporting response in the bundle.

States the three families (d.144.1.7/88854, d.144.1.6/64411, d.144.1.4/56171) share superfamily d.144.1 in fold d.144, release 2.08; sibling families and sunids match the children response. Superfamily read as probable common ancestry inferred from structure/mechanism; shared phosphotransfer scaffold with non-conserved acceptor chemistry; warns against assuming canonical kinase motifs (DFG, activation loop) map onto APH or PI3K. Explicitly refuses substrate and regulation transfer, and correctly notes that protein-level node 419100 is the d.15.15.1 ABD, not the catalytic domain (beta-grasp labelled as pretrained knowledge, which is correct). Requires kinetics/substrate panels, complex structures or mutagenesis, and regulatory partner data; notes domain architecture dependence. Complete and supported. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.
